question: Can an LLM perform derivative-free optimization by conditioning on a natural-language history of candidate solutions and their objective values?

key_findings.claim: OPRO repeatedly asks an optimizer LLM for new solutions from a meta-prompt containing the task, prior candidates, and their scores, then evaluates and appends those solutions without updating model weights.
key_findings.evidence: The loop is instantiated on linear regression, traveling-salesperson problems, and discrete instruction search; ordering candidates from low to high scores and retaining trajectory information are central design choices.

key_findings.claim: In prompt optimization, the best reported OPRO instructions outperform human prompts by up to 8 percentage points on GSM8K and up to 50 points on selected BBH tasks, with substantial dependence on optimizer/scorer model and meta-prompt.
key_findings.evidence: The experiments evaluate PaLM 2 variants and API models, while ablations show that candidate order, displayed scores, exemplars, and sampling temperature change convergence and final accuracy.

key_findings.claim: OPRO remains sensitive to wording, initialization, finite training samples, and optimizer capability; training-test gaps of roughly 5--20 points occur in reported prompt searches.
key_findings.evidence: Semantically similar prompts vary sharply, validation trends generally track training but overfitting persists, and concurrent EvoPrompt comparisons depend on task-specific initial prompts and exemplars.

method.core_idea: Represent a black-box optimization trajectory as text and exploit an LLM's in-context pattern extrapolation to propose better candidates.
method.mechanism: Seed a meta-prompt with candidate-score pairs and task examples, sample one or more new candidates, score them with an external objective or scorer LLM, and iteratively retain the trajectory within the context window.
assumptions: Candidate solutions and objective feedback fit into a prompt and are meaningful to the optimizer LLM.
The objective evaluation is sufficiently reliable to rank noisy candidates.
The task's search structure overlaps patterns the LLM can infer in context.

techniques.role: Turns scored optimization history into an LLM meta-prompt.
Balances exploitation and exploration by sampling from prior scored solutions.
Uses task accuracy as a black-box objective for prompt wording.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic linear regression, small traveling-salesperson instances, GSM8K, and 23 Big-Bench Hard tasks.
evaluations.metric: Objective value or tour length; training and test task accuracy of the scorer model under optimized instructions.
evaluations.result: OPRO improves candidates over iterations and finds instructions exceeding selected human-written baselines, but exhibits optimizer/model sensitivity and nontrivial overfitting.
evaluations.baseline: Random generation, heuristic TSP methods, zero-shot and chain-of-thought prompts, human instructions, one-step generation, and EvoPrompt variants.

limitations: Repeated scoring is inference- and data-intensive, and cost is not normalized against alternative search methods.
The strongest results use proprietary models, limiting exact reproduction and making model-version drift relevant.
Optimizing a small training set can overfit and exploit scorer idiosyncrasies.
Context length bounds the usable trajectory and high-dimensional numerical problems are represented with lossy text.
failure_modes: A weak optimizer LLM repeats or paraphrases candidates without useful exploration.
Noisy or hackable scores steer the search toward brittle prompts.
Semantically tiny wording changes can cause large performance oscillations.
Poor initialization or absent task exemplars can trap the trajectory.
reusable_insights: Natural-language optimizers should be evaluated as search algorithms, including cost, variance, and held-out objective performance.
Showing both candidates and scalar feedback can enable in-context optimization without parameter updates.
Error-case feedback may be more informative than a single aggregate score, but needs robust summarization.
open_questions: How does OPRO scale with problem dimension, context compression, and evaluation noise?
Can uncertainty-aware acquisition or explicit diversity improve exploration efficiency?
How should prompt optimization defend against validation overfitting and scorer reward hacking?

competitive_landscape.title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct predecessor for LLM-generated and scored instructions (APE).
competitive_landscape.difference: APE generates and iteratively refines prompt candidates; OPRO generalizes the pattern into trajectory-conditioned black-box optimization and tests non-prompt problems.

competitive_landscape.title: Connecting Large Language Models with Evolutionary Algorithms Yields Powerful Prompt Optimizers
competitive_landscape.difference: EvoPrompt explicitly asks for mutation and crossover of selected parents; OPRO provides a scored trajectory and lets the LLM infer an update strategy.

competitive_landscape.title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement Via Prompt Evolution
competitive_landscape.difference: Promptbreeder co-evolves task prompts and mutation prompts in a population; OPRO uses a simpler sequential meta-prompt with candidate scores.

novelty_assessment: OPRO's clearest novelty is treating an LLM plus scored textual trajectory as a generic optimizer and demonstrating it beyond prompt engineering. It overlaps prior automatic prompt search and concurrent evolutionary prompt work; evidence for generic numerical optimization is limited to small illustrative problems.
